item.text: {"question_id":"8B.9","answer":"During 2023, Tshisekedi actively managed the eastern crisis through security coordination, regional and international diplomacy, monetary directives, and a review of the state of siege. These actions show formal direction and some willingness to revise arrangements: he coordinated FARDC, MONUSCO, and EAC planning, sought AU and ICC engagement, directed named institutions to implement exchange-rate measures, and convened an evaluation of the state of siege (BATCH-0021-E001; BATCH-0021-E006; BATCH-0019-E001; BATCH-0024-E005; BATCH-0021-E012). However, the record does not show that these responses preserved or advanced the principal security objective. The EAC mandate produced no measurable security improvement according to the cited assessment, M23 retained or recaptured territory, and renewed fighting displaced more than 450,000 people in late 2023 (BATCH-0011-E016; BATCH-0011-E017; BATCH-0013-E014). Crisis and resistance management also generated serious implementation and accountability failures: the state’s militarized response to the planned Wazalendo protest was preplanned through provincial and military orders, followed by killings, mass arrests, disputed casualty reporting, inadequate investigation, and flawed prosecutions, although the supplied evidence assigns operational authority primarily to Governor and Military Operations Commander Constant Ndima rather than proving Tshisekedi personally ordered the operation (BATCH-0011-E018; BATCH-0011-E019; BATCH-0011-E020; BATCH-0011-E021; BATCH-0011-E022). More broadly, authorities restricted opposition, media, and peaceful protest, while the election process was chaotic and widely challenged, weakening durable political control and institutional legitimacy even though Tshisekedi was preliminarily declared the winner (BATCH-0010-E012; BATCH-0019-E012; BATCH-0028-E015). Overall, the evidence supports active and sometimes adaptive crisis response, but mixed-to-poor preservation of core security and accountability objectives; regional conflict, armed-group action, and international-force constraints materially limit direct attribution for the military stalemate and displacement.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0021-E001","BATCH-0021-E006","BATCH-0019-E001","BATCH-0024-E005","BATCH-0021-E012"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0011-E016","BATCH-0011-E017","BATCH-0013-E014","BATCH-0011-E018","BATCH-0011-E019","BATCH-0011-E020","BATCH-0011-E021","BATCH-0011-E022","BATCH-0010-E012","BATCH-0019-E012","BATCH-0028-E015","BATCH-0007-E008"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Formal meetings, diplomatic appeals, and ICC cooperation establish decisions and intended responses, not successful preservation or advancement of objectives.","The supplied evidence does not establish Tshisekedi’s personal authorization of the Goma operation or every subordinate abuse; operational authority is documented most directly for Governor and Military Operations Commander Constant Ndima.","The security outcomes were shaped by M23, Rwanda, other armed groups, regional rivalries, MONUSCO, EAC and SADC forces, and broader humanitarian shocks.","The supplied passages do not establish the implementation or effects of the monetary measures, the conclusions of the state-of-siege review, or the long-term durability of the cited responses."],"corrections_made":["Reduced the positive weight assigned to meetings, diplomatic appeals, and ICC cooperation by distinguishing formal response from demonstrated effectiveness.","Added the preplanned Goma operation, inadequate investigations, disputed casualty handling, flawed civilian prosecutions, and limited accountability as material crisis-management failures.","Corrected attribution by separating Ndima’s documented operational authority from unproven personal presidential authorization.","Preserved mixed evidence, including security coordination, adaptive review, and some convictions, without treating them as proof of successful crisis resolution."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":["Further review would be warranted if evidence directly links national authorities or Tshisekedi personally to the Goma orders, subsequent corrective action, or accountability decisions.","Further implementation and outcome evidence could clarify whether monetary stabilization, the state-of-siege review, election management, and regional-force replacement advanced durable objectives.","Additional independent evidence could better separate Tshisekedi’s choices from regional actors’ refusal or inability to conduct the expected military operations."]}
